comments.body:
Root cause confirmed and fix committed locally (b98e8e0b036, not yet pushed).

Observation: the copied cross-process repro (starve2.py) timed out the writer at 3.02-3.05 s in 3 of 3 runs with all yield probes False. Adding one 0.25 s pause between release and probe let the writer in at 0.54-0.60 s in 3 of 3. The lock is an unqueued polling lock (waiter polls every 37-62 ms in a pass, up to 2.5 s backoff between passes), so a release-probe-retake within microseconds always wins.

Fix: `_give_waiters_a_turn` in `_run_sweep` pauses after each fold for the waiter's poll gap plus 0.5 s (about 0.63 s), or the backoff cap plus 0.5 s (3 s) after a fold of 1 s or more; gap values come from new constants in `lock.py` that the poll loops use. `_sweep_one_ticket` pushes each fold (best-effort). No new lock, env var, or config key.

Tests (`tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_handover.py`, 6): the cross-process writer test and the per-fold publish test fail on old code 3 of 3 (writer `timeout 2.0x`; unpushed counts [1, 2]) and all 6 pass 3 of 3 on the fix. Regression: 22 compaction/lock/concurrency/push modules, 267 passed, 2 skipped. make lint and make typecheck exit 0. make verify running next.

Filed bug breezelike-travelsick-moray (discovered_from) for single folds that hold the lock 100-165 s, which this fix does not shorten.

compiled_state.description:
## What is wrong

The compaction sweep's stand-aside check cannot see a writer that is waiting for the store write lock, so a long sweep starves canonical writes until they time out.

`_sweep_should_yield` (`src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`) calls `write_lock_is_busy` between tickets. At that moment the sweep has just released the lock, so the probe reports "not busy" unless the waiting writer happened to win the race in that instant. The sweep then takes the lock for the next ticket. A writer polling with its 181 s budget (30 s x 2 attempts x 3 passes) keeps losing.

## Evidence

Production MCP host, 2026-11-01 21:00-21:35 PST (journald `rebar-mcp`, read-only SSM):

- One sweep (`op=compact-sweep`, pid 1427) committed 10 `COMPACT` events between 21:03:13 and 21:34:49, holding the lock 100-165 s per ticket.
- A waiting writer's retry log shows the holder's `held=` fall from 161 s to 25 s within one wait: the sweep released and re-took the lock while the writer was still waiting.
- 3 writes failed with `flock: could not acquire lock after 181s ... op=compact-sweep`: a plan-review attestation at 21:08:30, and 2 `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecars at 21:10:36 and 21:11:32. That lost a billed PASS (`b505-d66e-86b3-4446`) and a billed BLOCK's findings (`2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9`).
- The build that ran included `f3cb9223d8c` (bug `graspable-fabled-skylark`, history walks moved out of the lock), so this is a different path to the same outage.

Local reproduction (current main, real `rebar._store.lock`, separate processes): a holder loop that holds for 1 s, releases, calls `write_lock_is_busy`, and re-takes the lock. A writer in another process waits with a 3 s budget. Result: writer `LockTimeout` after 3.03 s; all 6 yield probes returned `False`.

## Second effect: real divergence for the length of the sweep

The sweep commits each fold locally and pushes once at the end ("Pushes remain batched"). On the host clone, `HEAD` gained 10 unpushed `COMPACT` commits while fetches fast-forwarded `origin/tickets` 4 times. From 21:06:15 to the 21:35:01 merge the clone had genuinely diverged, so every gate's freshness check correctly refused with `stale-store` for about 29 minutes.

## Root cause (confirmed)

The store lock is an unqueued polling lock. A waiting writer re-polls the kernel leg every 37-62 ms and the mkdir leg every 75-125 ms within a pass, and sleeps up to 2.5 s (jittered backoff cap) between passes. The sweep releases, probes, and re-takes within microseconds, so a polling waiter almost never observes the lock free and the probe almost never observes the waiter. Experiment (copied repro, 3 runs each): unchanged holder, writer timed out at 3.02-3.05 s in 3 of 3; same holder with a 0.25 s pause between release and probe, writer acquired at 0.54-0.60 s in 3 of 3.

## Approach

1. Hand the lock over before re-taking it. In `_run_sweep`, after each ticket and before the next `_sweep_should_yield` probe, the sweep stays off the lock for longer than the longest gap in which a waiter is not polling: the within-pass poll gap plus a scheduling margin (about 0.6 s) after a short fold, and the between-pass backoff gap plus the margin (about 3 s) after a fold that ran 1 s or more (the shortest pass budget any `acquire` caller can set, since `timeout` is whole seconds), because only then can a waiter have exhausted a pass and be in backoff. A waiting writer takes the lock in that window; the probe then reads busy and the sweep yields as designed. The gap values come from new named constants in `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` that the poll loops themselves use, so the two cannot drift. No new lock, env var, config key, or flag; `_sweep_should_yield` keeps its signature.
2. Publish each fold. `_sweep_one_ticket` calls `push.push_after_commit` (best-effort, after the fold's lock is released, honouring `sync.push`) when a fold committed a new SNAPSHOT and `--no-commit` is off. The end-of-run `_commit_backfill` push stays as the safety net. This replaces the "pushes remain batched" cadence from bug `prone-octet-cheek`, whose goal (no stranded commits) this keeps; the cost is one push per folded ticket in an out-of-band sweep.

Out of scope: a single fold that itself holds the lock longer than a writer's whole budget (production folds held 100-165 s against a 181 s budget). That is a per-fold hold limit, not the hand-over defect; bug `breezelike-travelsick-moray` tracks it.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/lock.py`: named poll and backoff constants used by `_acquire_fcntl`, `_acquire_mkdir`, and `acquire`; a public `max_waiter_gap_s(between_passes)` helper.
- `src/rebar/_commands/compact.py`: `_give_waiters_a_turn` pause in `_run_sweep`; per-fold push in `_sweep_one_ticket`.
- `tests/unit/test_compact_sweep_handover.py` (new): the tests below.

## Testing

- Cross-process (AC 1): a holder process loop of real `rebar._store.lock` holds of 0.3 s that calls the real `_give_waiters_a_turn` and `_sweep_should_yield` between holds; a writer subprocess with a 3 s budget must acquire. Subprocesses are bounded with `communicate(timeout=...)` and killed in `finally`. Fails on the old code (writer times out).
- Unit: after a fold of 1 s or more the pause is at least the between-pass gap, after a short fold at least the within-pass gap, and no pause precedes the first ticket.
- Unit: a waiter that takes the lock during the pause makes the sweep yield (real lock, other process).
- AC 2: a sweep of 3 tickets against a bare origin; at every between-ticket probe the local tickets branch has no commits absent from origin. Fails on the old code. `--no-commit` makes no push.
- Regression: the full compaction and concurrency modules (`tests/unit/test_compact*.py`, `tests/unit/test_write_lock*.py`, `tests/unit/test_lock*.py`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_inline_write_push.py`, `tests/integration/test_concurrency_regression.py`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A writer waiting for the store lock while the sweep runs gets the lock before its budget expires. Checked by: test with a sweep-like holder in one process and a waiting writer in another, asserting the writer acquires the lock.
- [ ] The sweep's unpublished folds do not leave the clone diverged from the shared store for longer than one fold. Checked by: test asserting the clone has no unpushed sweep commits after each fold when the push target is reachable.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.
